ILLUSTRATIVE DATA
Passport no. · Barcode · Mould

Follow this piece from source to doorstep. Every piece in the collection follows the same standards: 999 gold from an accredited refinery, due diligence in line with the OECD guidance for mineral supply chains, independent yearly audits of suppliers, and a batch code () that follows each material to the finished piece.

TRACEABILITY

Each piece is tested by X-ray fluorescence, weighed and measured against its mould (), then checked under magnification for finish and setting. The assay for this piece reads parts per thousand. A serial number links the piece to barcode and its certificate.
The piece is packed in a presentation box with its certificate of authenticity, sealed with a tamper-evident label and delivered insured to your Singapore address. Delivery is free, and a signature is required on receipt.

THE STORY OF CTF • PALACE MUSEUM

A HERITAGE OF FIRSTS

  1. 1929Chow Tai Fook is founded in Guangzhou.
  2. 1972First to launch 999.9 gold jewellery in Hong Kong and Macao.
  3. 1990Introduces its “Fixed Price” policy: the price on the tag is the final price.
  4. 2014Master Studio begins working with the Chinese University of Hong Kong to study historic goldworking techniques.
  5. 2016Launches T•MARK, bringing traceability to its diamonds.
  6. 2023Begins a strategic partnership with the Palace Museum in Beijing.
  7. 2024Launches the Palace Museum Collection.
Free Singapore delivery

Terms and Conditions

Packaging

Your piece arrives in a Chow Tai Fook presentation box, wrapped in tissue and closed with a tamper-evident label.

The box contains a certificate of authenticity, a care card and a polishing cloth. Gift wrapping and a handwritten message card are available at checkout.

Delivery

Free Singapore delivery on all online orders.

Orders are dispatched within 2 to 3 working days and delivered by insured courier. A signature is required on receipt, so please choose an address where someone can accept the parcel.

Collection from selected Singapore stores is available at checkout.

BEHIND THE PIECE

The Palace Museum Collection: from imperial artefacts to the goldsmith's bench

The collection turns objects and paintings from the Forbidden City into gold jewellery made with ancient techniques. See where the ideas come from, then follow the making in six stages.
